priced_in_evidence.claim_scope: Scheduled FOMC decisions listed on Kalshi, March 2022 to October 2026
priced_in_evidence.headline: Kalshi's expected rate change before each meeting and the fed-funds-futures surprise measured by the San Francisco Fed agree closely (correlation 0.85 over 32 meetings, against 0.32 for the raw rate change), so the decision itself is mostly in prices before 2 pm. How much of the remaining move belongs to the decision could not be measured: on FOMC days guidance moves prices more than the decision.
priced_in_evidence.details: The preregistered test also required the futures surprise to move one-for-one with the Kalshi surprise; it moved 0.25 times as much (90% interval 0.23–0.28), partly because the front-month futures change is a monthly average, so that test failed. Models that tried to predict the outcome-specific move from 2022–2024 meetings did not beat an outcome-blind range on 2024–2026 meetings (1 of 15 portfolios; the shipped published transfer 5 of 15).
priced_in_evidence.long_sample_test: A second preregistered test on 112 earlier FOMC meetings (fitted 2008–2014, tested on 56 meetings in 2015–2022, fed-funds-futures surprise) found the outcome shift this card uses pointing the right way for 9 of 10 portfolios, both intraday and on the day (daily improvement +0.9%, 90% interval +0.1% to +1.6%), but too small to pass the 2% bar: the average surprise was about 1 bp. The shift is real but small next to the release-day range.
priced_in_evidence.what_it_does_not_show: This does not identify the share of an FOMC-day move caused by the decision, does not convert Kalshi prices into physical probabilities, and does not apply to unscheduled events.
priced_in_evidence.probability_calibration: Kalshi's rate ladders were sharp: across 190 strike forecasts (Brier score 0.0033), no outcome priced at 5% or less happened and every outcome priced at 95% or more did.

calibration.naive_definition: P(X>k) = share of the previous 24 realized releases above k (needs 12)

priced_in_evidence.headline: Before each of the 56 Kalshi-listed CPI releases since November 2021, stock and bond prices already reflected Kalshi's expected print: only the gap between the actual print and that expectation moved them (share of the expectation already in prices: 1.02 for SPY, 90% interval 0.89–1.13; 1.08 for IEF, 0.97–1.18). priced_in_evidence.details: Method: for every release, Kalshi's last pre-release quotes give the expected print; each security's move from the prior close to 10:00 ET is regressed on actual − λ·expected − (1−λ)·previous print, and λ is profiled (1 = fully anticipated, 0 = nothing anticipated). In a separate regression the anticipated change itself had no measurable effect (SPY coefficient 0.0016 ± 0.0041). A preregistered attempt to predict the size of each outcome's move from 2021–2024 data failed on 2024–2026 releases (0 of 15 test portfolios beat an outcome-blind range): SPY moved 0.62% per 0.1 pp of CPI surprise in 2021–2024 but only 0.08% in 2024–2026. The release-day range therefore matters more than the outcome-specific shift.
priced_in_evidence.long_sample_test: A preregistered test on 98 earlier CPI releases (2013–2021, Cleveland Fed nowcast as the expectation) failed: in that period CPI surprises did not move these portfolios measurably (the shipped shift was worse than an outcome-blind range on all 14 testable portfolios intraday). CPI became market-moving only in the 2021–2024 inflation period.
priced_in_evidence.what_it_does_not_show: This is not a claim that Kalshi prices are physical probabilities, it is a full-sample estimate rather than an out-of-sample test, and it rests mostly on the 2021–2024 inflation period: on 2024–2026 releases alone CPI surprises moved stocks too little to measure the share (it stays measurable only for the Treasury fund IEF, 1.07 with 90% interval 0.49–1.5). It does not apply to unscheduled geopolitical events or identify how much of a stock's value depends on the event.
priced_in_evidence.probability_calibration: Kalshi's CPI ladders were well calibrated: across 429 strike forecasts, outcomes priced at 5–20% happened 10% of the time and those priced at 80–95% happened 86%; they beat a history-based forecast in 84% of releases.
